0.0.n: Combines with ご飯 to make 朝ご飯, the word for breakfast.

0.1.n: ご飯 can mean rice or a meal; here it completes 朝ご飯, breakfast.

0.2.n: Links breakfast to 次, identifying what the next activity follows.

0.3.n: 次に places this activity after breakfast in the routine.

0.4.n: With 次, marks when the activity happens.

0.5.n: する becomes している, which describes a regular habit here rather than an action happening right now.

0.6.n: Turns している into a noun phrase: the thing the speaker does.

0.7.n: Marks the whole phrase about what the speaker does after breakfast as the topic.

0.9.n: Specifies the time associated with the stretches.

0.10.n: Links 朝 to ストレッチ, describing the stretches as part of the morning routine.

0.11.n: This borrowed word refers to physical stretching exercises.

0.12.n: Politely identifies the after-breakfast activity as morning stretches.

1.0.n: Names the activity the speaker says these stretches are not.

1.1.n: This で belongs to でもない, a negative expression after a noun; it does not mark location.

1.2.n: Adds the sense of also rejecting yoga as a label for the activity.

1.3.n: ない makes the statement negative, and です adds politeness.

1.4.n: Softens the statement and gently invites the listener to share the speaker's view.

2.0.n: Serves as the comparison point for how serious the exercise is.

2.1.n: Marks yoga as a level of seriousness the speaker's routine does not reach.

2.2.n: Describes a fully developed practice, contrasting with the speaker's simpler stretching routine.

2.3.n: Connects 本格的 to the noun こと so it can describe that noun.

2.4.n: Refers generally to an activity rather than a physical object.

2.5.n: Highlights serious activities as the category the speaker does not do.

2.6.n: The negative of している describes what is not part of the speaker's regular routine.

2.7.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone before です.

2.8.n: Makes the explanation polite as part of んです.

2.9.n: Politely introduces a contrast, leaving the sentence open for the next line.

3.0.n: This is the name of the video platform.

3.1.n: Links YouTube to ビデオ, identifying the platform the videos come from.

3.2.n: Japanese nouns usually do not distinguish singular from plural.

3.3.n: Marks the videos as what the speaker watches.

3.4.n: The stem of 見る, formed by removing る, attaches to ながら.

3.5.n: After a verb stem, shows an action happening alongside the main action.

3.7.n: Identifies the time associated with the stretching routine.

3.8.n: Connects 朝 with ストレッチ to describe morning stretches.

3.9.n: Refers to stretching exercises, which are the main activity in this sentence.

3.10.n: Marks ストレッチ as the activity performed with やっています.

3.11.n: Gives the duration of the stretching session without needing a separate particle.

3.12.n: Makes the ten-minute duration approximate rather than exact.

3.13.n: Limits the duration, emphasizing that the routine takes little time.

3.14.n: やる becomes やっている, with polite ます; here it describes a habit.

0.lit: As for what I regularly do next after breakfast, it is morning stretching.
0.tip: していること turns an action into a noun phrase meaning what the speaker does.

1.lit: It is not yoga either, you know.
1.tip: でもない rejects a noun as a description; here the speaker says yoga is not quite the right label.

2.lit: As for anything serious to the level of yoga, I do not do it, but…
2.tip: んです adds an explanatory tone, while けれども leads into the contrasting description that follows.

3.lit: While watching YouTube videos, I do morning stretches for only about ten minutes.
3.tip: A verb stem plus ながら means while doing that action; the main action comes later.
